description: Authored safety judgment. The generator and independent clap-surface tests consume this policy; runtime notices continue to consume generated commands.json, so stale metadata cannot be silently repaired at runtime.

destructive_commands.deploy apply: Deployment can replace existing definitions and delete items. The concrete plan still reports whether its selected actions are destructive.
destructive_commands.dataflow upgrade-gen1: Execution always replaces the selected Gen1 items irreversibly. The approval flag gates execution; it does not make an otherwise harmless mode destructive.
destructive_commands.data-agent upload-topic: PUT can permanently replace an existing topic; ETag preconditions prevent concurrent replacement but do not make replacement reversible.
destructive_commands.workspace modify-file-soft-delete: Disabling retention or reducing its duration changes recovery guarantees for future file deletions; already deleted files retain their original expiry.

non_destructive_commands.workspace reset-shortcut-cache: Clears an ephemeral shortcut cache, not the underlying data or definitions.
non_destructive_commands.sql-database stop-mirroring: Pauses replication; it does not delete the mirrored data or cancel an arbitrary running query.
non_destructive_commands.mirrored-database stop: Pauses mirroring and can be reversed with start; it does not delete the database.
non_destructive_commands.reflex stop-rule: Disables a rule; the rule definition is retained and can be started again.
non_destructive_commands.operations-agent stop: Sets shouldRun=false while retaining the agent definition.
non_destructive_commands.deploy plan: Read-only planning accepts deployment safety options to describe future actions; it never applies them.
